4. Vertebrata (L; vertebratus-jointed)
A vertebrate can be defined as an animal of phylum chordata having bony or cartilaginous endoskeleton that consists of cranium enclosing brain and a vertebral column enclosing a nerve cord.
General characters:

1. Lower vertebrates are aquatic and higher vertebrates are terrestrial. 2. Body is usually divisible into head, neck, trunk and post-anal tail. 3. Their exoskeleton consists of protective scales, feather, hair found in skin. Nail, claws,

hoof, horn etc. are also found. 4. Skin or integument is differentiated into epidermis and dermis along with cutaneous glands. 5. Notochord in the early embryonic stage is replaced by cartilaginous or bony vertebral column in adult. 6. Endoskeleton is either cartilaginous or bony where muscles are attached. 7. They have well developed organ systems.
Sub-phylum vertebrata is further divided into two divisions:
Division 1. Agnatha (Gr; a-not; gnatha-jaw): Division agnatha comprises jawless vertebrates which consists of only one class called cyclostomata (Gr; cyclos-circular; stomamouth).
Characters i. They are exclusively aquatic forms, mostly found in marine water. Mostly parasitic or scavengerous. ii. Body is elongated and eel-shaped.

iii. Their appendages are unpaired. iv. Skin is soft, smooth and slimy without scales. v. Mouth is circular and suctorial. vi. They have single nostril and 5-16 pairs of gills. vii. Heart two chambered. viii. Sexes are separate or united, gonad single and fertilization is external.
Example: Petromyzon (lamprey), Myxine (hag fish) etc.

Figure 8.2.21 Petromyzon Division 2: Gnathostomata (Gr; gnatha-jaw; stoma-mouth; ata-form): This division constitutes jawed vertebrates. It has two super classes; Pisces and Tetrapoda Super class 1: Pisces (L; piscis-fish) It includes all the fishes which are essentially aquatic having 3 main characters such as body streamlined and covered with scales, respiration by gills, paired fins for locomotion.

Characters: 1. They are always aquatic, freshwater or marine form. 2. Body is streamlined or spindle shaped and divisible into head, trunk and tail. Neck is absent. 3. Locomotion takes place by paired pectoral and pelvic fins; unpaired median dorsal fin and tail fin. Muscular tail acts as propeller and rudder. 4. Body is externally covered by waterproof dermal scales with some exceptions. 5. Their endoskeleton is either bony or cartilaginous. 6. Respiration mainly takes place through gills and gills are naked or covered by operculum. Presence of 5-7 pairs of gill slits. 7. Alimentary canal is a complete tube terminating into cloaca or anus. 8. Their heart is 2 chambered with blood vessels and blood. RBC nucleated. 9. They are poikilothermic i.e. body temperature gets fluctuated according to surrounding environment. 10. Kidneys are mesonephric and excretion is ammonotelic or ureotelic. 11. Nervous system comprises brain, spinal cord and nerves where cranial nerves are 10 paired. Sensory organs are nasal sac for olfaction, auditory apparatus, lateral line system etc. 12. Sexes are separate and fertilization is external or internal. Female is oviparous (eggs large and yolky) or ovoviviparous and development is usually direct. Unique features Exclusively aquatic, gill breather, body covered by waterproof scales, locomotion by fins, heart two chambered, poikilothermic, cranial nerves 10 pairs Biology, Grade 11 | 342

Super class pisces is broadly divided into 2 classes. Class 1: Elasmobranchi or Chondrichthyes (Gr; chondros-cartilage; ichthys-fish) i. They are marine and predatory fishes. ii. Skin is tough with minute placoid scales and some naked with mucous glands. iii. Tail is hetercercal. iv. They have cartilaginous endoskeleton. v. Their mouth is ventral in position. vi. Respiration occurs through 5-7 pairs of gills and gill slits are not covered by operculum. vii. They have no swim bladder viii. Fertilization is internal; male has claspers at the base of pelvic fins to transfer sperm into the genital tract of female. They are ovoviviparous. Example: Scoliodon (dog fish), Trygon (sting ray), Torpedo (electric ray), Chimaera (rat fish) etc.
